findings.text: follow-on: the fragment's mechanism bullet is titled 'The state that inflates it' and states the two-carrier interleave as the cause, but the plan lists that as a lead ('Leads, not conclusions. The node decides which of these holds, if any.') and the fragment's own carrier table and opencheck show the state cannot be reconstructed now; the load-bearing fact is left unstated: it says 'every key move starts a new run' without naming which key component moves, yet an alternation between two carriers of one job splits a run only if their run key differs. On disk the raw rows carry boot_id=null while the compacted tiers carry a real boot_id (deepseek-v4-1-flash-1280470.jsonl has hostname=98dci4-gpu-0003.iter.org, boot_id=None; .hour.jsonl and .minute.jsonl carry boot_id=58cc3b8e-66b3-4b4f-baf3-e9e8b8f7c406), which is exactly the key difference that would make each alternation a new run. The fragment does not say this, so a reader cannot reproduce the split from the fragment alone.

follow-on: the fragment reports '63 hour rows and 3,672 minute rows' as a fixed count of the live job 1280470's compacted tiers, but the minute tier is an actively growing file (3,682 rows at review time, mtime 10:33Z). A count that moves under the reader should be timestamped or bounded; the hour count (63) is stable, the minute count is not.

follow-on: the ingest-log sentence reads 'the neighbouring hundred-and-nineteenth ticks read one file (07:22:01Z ... read=1, 07:24:05Z ... read=1)', which is garbled prose; the intent (the ticks immediately before and after the read=3 tick) is recoverable from the log but the phrase as written is not readable.

follow_ons: the two-carrier run split would be reproducible if the fragment stated the key difference it rests on: the raw carrier rows carry no boot_id while the compacted tiers carry a real one, so the run key (host, boot_id, job_id) moves on every alternation.

The worker correctly wrote the fragment the done-when names; the template line is the defect (the done-when does name an artifact).
